answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money — sparingly and against verified performance — so Sybil inflation is filtered before it compounds. Consider a horizon at the center, a ocean resting nearby, and a sonnet beyond the hills: three anchors, none forged, all earned over time.
